author: potuz
content:
FWIW, as I said in 201, what I think needs to happen is that up to an even during the P fork we need to keep the current deposit contract as a way to onboard new PQ validators before the Q fork: validators deposit and immediately preregister. 

During this time we can also deploy two new deposit contracts for PQ validators and PQ builders, that won't take anything until the fork itself. 

At the Q fork we need to stop processing deposit requests from the original deposits (or if we process them just refund them immediately) and start accepting deposits only from the two new contracts.

author: .vshvsh
content:
> What I like of the current preregistration proposal, in the current exact form, is that it works for key rotation, something pools have requested multiple times. cc @vsh
to give a bit of context - I think almost all node operators to be compromised in a years' time. Currently if a node operator is compromised and knows it, they have a choice of
- rotating the validator key through exit/entry or consolidations
-- slow: these queues can be months long
-- expensive - lose a decent amount of staking rewards which will reflect on their relationships with stakers.
- run with compromised keys and hope that nothing bad happens

We don't actually know how often second option happens but I expect it to happen more often than we'd consider safe. Incentives are perverse.

if they don't know it, they will only key rotate once in consolidations, if even that. Regular rotation out of precaution just doesn't exist.


almost-free option for key rotation would be hugely beneficial for netwrok safety because it removes the perverse incentives of running with compromised keys and opens up a regular key rotation practice.

author: .vshvsh
content: in general I think it's better if rotation is entirely the purview of the node operator (so happens on beacon chain, not by execution request initiated by the staker) because staker-initiated is extra friction that would hamper adoption; execution message is better than status quo by a lot so I'd take it

author: .vshvsh
content: but ideally it's just node operator rotation validation keys they manage

author: wemeetagain
content:
regarding https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5770
Instead of bringing the eth1hash check to the CL,
We could instead add `payload_root` to the bid, and then check that in the gossip rule.

author: nc1234
content:
I think this is better. One concern is it also introduces container change this late in the process instead of just updating gossip validation. Also payload_root check also needs to be performed when we receive payload envelope. 
(ssz blocks fixes this btw)

author: wemeetagain
content:
Yeah its a consensus breaking change (container change). That breaks compat with sepolia.
The payload_root is already computed for the (now mostly useless) signature check.

author: wemeetagain
content:
But commiting to a specific payload in the bid and checking that commitment during gossip is kinda the entire point of PR in any case.
The idea behind `payload_root` in bid is just to use the same commitment scheme and machinery we use everywhere else in the consensus-specs.
